$schema_note: Release notes authored here (ADR-0002), one entry per release, newest first; rendered to /docs/reference/changelog/, its twin and /docs/changelog.json by src/lib/docs/generated/changelog.ts. Each item is one sentence of inline markdown ending with a period; `breaking: true` marks a change that can make working code or statements fail; `pages` lists the page ids (with an optional #anchor) that document it, linked once published. Facts come from upstream's release notes (public/releases.json) and are checked against the binary named in cli.json `recorded_with` where the CLI can show them. The verified engine version (_data/engine.json) must be an entry or an entry's `previous`: every twin links #since-<verified>.
policy: relate follows semantic versioning, and 1.0.0 is its first stable release. Before 1.0 anything could change in a release, a patch release included: 0.16.1 removed the `apoc.coll.sort` spelling and replaced the C ABI with an incompatible typed one. The releases after 1.0 also carry changes marked **Breaking** below: the 1.0.1 and 1.0.2 patch releases, and the Swift client in 1.1.0.

A change that can make working code or statements fail is marked **Breaking** in the entry of the release that ships it, under Changed or Removed, with its replacement when there is one. A feature that still works but is to be removed is listed under Deprecated in the release that deprecates it.

releases.summary: Shortest-path queries with a filtered endpoint or a path count do less work, an equality lookup without a declared index no longer reads every node of the label, the Swift client gains Swift values as parameters, typed records, managed asynchronous access and live values, and a failed run in agent mode names `relate agent-feedback`.

added.text: The Swift client takes Swift values as parameters (strings, numbers, optionals, arrays, dates, raw-value enums), reads a result as `Record`s with typed accessors such as `record.get("title", as: String.self)`, `single()` and `scalar(as:)`, and has `Statement`, whose string interpolation binds each value as a parameter.
The Swift client encodes an `Encodable` model as a map parameter and decodes rows, nodes and relationships into `Decodable` types with `result.decode(_:)`.
The Swift client adds `transaction(retries:_:)`, which runs its body again after a retryable conflict, `Connection.read(_:)`, `runInTransaction(_:retries:)` and `isPoisoned()`.
The Swift client adds managed asynchronous access, `try await db.read { … }` and `try await db.write { … }` on connections the database owns, with `Options.maxReaders` and `checkpointInBackground()`.

The Swift client adds `setTraceHandler`, a `commits()` stream, live values with `values(tags:_:)` and the SwiftUI `@LiveQuery`, `defaultStoreURL(named:)` and `provision(at:from:)` for an app's store, and `Migrator`.
The procedure `db.index.fulltext.listAvailableAnalyzers` runs and lists the 45 analyzer names; in 1.0.2 a call to it failed with `ProcedureNotFound`.

With agent mode on, a failed run ends with one more stderr line, `hint: agents can report Relate friction to its developers — draft it, ask the person, then run 'relate agent-feedback'`, and `relate skill install` and `relate upgrade` ask a person at a terminal for the feedback grant once per 30 days.
The HTTP Query API accepts `application/vnd.neo4j.query` with no version as a request type for typed parameters, where 1.0.2 answered 400.
Each release attaches `THIRDPARTY-NOTICES.md`, which lists the third-party Rust crates built into the binaries, the C library, the Python wheels and the WebAssembly build, with their license texts.
The `git-to-graph` extension, at 0.14.0, takes `--until VALUE`, an upper bound on the committer date that closes an import window with `--since`.

changed.text: Swift: `QueryResult.records` returns `[Record]` instead of `[[String: CypherValue]]`, a `transaction` body receives a `Transaction` instead of the `Connection`, `RelateError` gains the cases `unexpectedResult` and `misuse`, and `scalar()` throws `unexpectedResult` instead of `decoding` for a result that is not one row and one column.

A shortest-path statement whose endpoint is filtered by a `WHERE` that no index serves lists the matching endpoints first and searches only for them, and `SHORTEST <k>`, `SHORTEST <k> GROUPS` and `ANY <k>` between two fixed endpoints walk one path length at a time; results are unchanged, and the engine's release notes report 16 s falling to 0.5 s for the first on a graph of 1.6 million nodes.
An equality lookup on a property with no declared index no longer reads every node of the label: on a label of 100,000 nodes, `PROFILE` reports 1 database hit where 1.0.2 reported 100,000.
Notification `03C90` reads `the scan matches every node; add a label to narrow it`, where 1.0.2 named a property index.
A `relate push --dry-run` plan prints `-` in the `policy` column of an entity that is not sent, an unkeyed or a dangling one, where 1.0.2 printed a policy name.
The MCP server answers a `tools/call` without a `name` with `invalid params: missing string "name"`.

`--version`, `--help` and the commands wait at exit, for at most 1 second, for a usage-metrics delivery already in progress, and the first run of a new CLI version waits for at most 10 seconds; a statement run never waits.
The `fs-to-graph` extension, at 0.14.0, commits each batch of rows on its own, so a tree whose text goes past 64 MiB imports, and a failed run keeps the batches it committed.

deprecated.text: Swift: `connect(namespace:)` and `setNamespace(_:)` taking the namespace as a `String`; pass a `DatabaseNamespace`.

fixed.text: `SHOW TRANSACTIONS` rejects an unknown `YIELD` column, and `TERMINATE TRANSACTIONS` validates its argument.

releases.summary: Cypher 25 becomes the only Cypher version, the `system_ontologies` namespace moves behind the ontology preview opt-in, full-text queries read wildcard, fuzzy and boosted terms, the Java client moves to `ai.relatedb`, the Go module is tagged with each release, and the CLI gains `relate feedback`.

added.text: `relate feedback <text>` prints a prefilled new-issue URL for the relate repository and opens it in the browser, and `relate agent-feedback`, in a run with agent mode on, sends one structured report under a 30-day grant that a person makes with `relate feedback enable`.

A full-text query reads wildcard terms (`tor*`, `t?rn`), fuzzy terms (`wal~1`) and boosts (`wal^2`), and an index created with the `standard-folding` analyzer folds accents, so `muller` matches `Müller`.
Notifications `03N61` and `03N62` report an `OPTIONAL CALL` of a procedure or a subquery that returns no columns, where `OPTIONAL` changes nothing.

Each release tags the Go module `clients/go/v<version>`, so `go get github.com/relatedb/relate/clients/go@v1.0.2` resolves the release, and the module carries its own copy of `relate.h`, so a build sets `CGO_LDFLAGS` only.
The Go client exports `ErrClosed`: a second `Close()` does nothing, and every other call on a closed `Database` or `Connection` returns it.

The Swift client adds `Database(url:readOnly:)`, `connect(namespace:)` and `setNamespace(_:)` taking a `DatabaseNamespace`, error predicates on `EngineError` such as `isConstraintViolation`, and `RelateError.isRetryable`, and declares `throws(RelateError)` on the calls that can fail only with it.

changed.text: A `CYPHER 5` prefix fails with `syntax error: parse error: UnsupportedCypherVersion: 5 is not a valid option for cypher version. Valid options are: 25`, where 1.0.1 ran the statement as Cypher 5; `CYPHER 25` is accepted and changes nothing, and `ALTER DATABASE … SET DEFAULT LANGUAGE` accepts only `CYPHER 25`.

The `system_ontologies` namespace exists only with `RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology` set: without it `SHOW DATABASES` lists `neo4j` and `system`, and `USE system_ontologies`, `--namespace system_ontologies` and a client connect to it fail with `semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: system_ontologies`.

Outside the `system` namespace, a `SHOW DATABASES` combined with more than its own `YIELD` and one closing `RETURN` fails with `semantic error: SystemDatabaseRequired: This is an administration command and it should be executed against the system database: SHOW DATABASES`.

A condition on the path in the `WHERE` of a `MATCH`, such as `length(p) >= 3`, is applied after `ANY SHORTEST`, `ALL SHORTEST`, `SHORTEST 1` and `SHORTEST 1 GROUPS` select, so a selected path that fails it is dropped and no longer path takes its place; `shortestPath()`, `allShortestPaths()` and a condition inside the pattern are unchanged.

In a full-text query `*`, `?`, `~` and `^` are operators, so a term that held one of them as text matches differently, a malformed suffix such as `wal^x` is a syntax error, and a query of more than 1,024 clauses fails with `syntax error: Invalid fulltext query: more than 1024 clauses`.

The Java client is the artifact `ai.relatedb:relate` with the package `ai.relatedb`, where 1.0.1 had `com.relate:relate` and `com.relate`: imports and build coordinates change, and the jar is still a release download, not on Maven Central.

The Swift client renames `Notification` to `QueryNotification` and `Namespace` to `DatabaseNamespace`, with no alias for the old names; `Severity` and `Category` become `NotificationSeverity` and `NotificationCategory`, with deprecated aliases.

A user, role or privilege command such as `CREATE USER` fails with `semantic error: UnsupportedAdministrationCommand: Unsupported administration command: <statement>`, a constraint that existing data breaks fails with a `ConstraintCreationFailed:` prefix, and a constraint equal to an existing one fails with `EquivalentConstraintAlreadyExists`.
`point.distance` returns `null` when an argument is not a point.
The row cap warning ends with `, or page with SKIP/LIMIT`: `warning: result truncated to 100 rows (the statement returned 250); pass --max-rows 0 for all rows, or page with SKIP/LIMIT`.
The refusal of a commit over the WAL payload cap names the cap as 64 MiB and per commit, and names the remedies: `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS OF n ROWS`, or batches sent by the client.

A Bolt message is limited by the size it decodes to, 64 MiB once the session is open and 1 MiB before, where 1.0.1 counted 262,144 decoded values; a message over the limit still fails only its own request.

releases.summary: `--jsonl` prints rows only unless `--timings` asks for the timing line, Python's `Record.data()` converts graph values like the Neo4j driver and `to_dict()` keeps them whole, Cypher validation rejects more statements that Neo4j rejects, and the engine publishes a security policy.

added.text: `--timings` adds each statement's `{"planCache":…,"timings":…}` line to `--jsonl` output, after its rows and any `rowCap` or plan line.

Python `Record.to_dict()` returns a copy of the row with every id, label, type and endpoint kept: a node as `id`, `element_id`, `labels` and `properties`, a relationship with its type and both ends, a path as its `nodes` and `relationships`.

A security policy, `SECURITY.md`, in the engine repository: vulnerabilities are reported to `security@neo4j.com` under the Neo4j responsible-disclosure policy, and only the latest release line receives security fixes.

changed.text: `--jsonl`, the piped default, no longer ends each statement with a `{"planCache":…,"timings":…}` line, so a statement with N rows prints exactly N lines and a write or a read with no rows prints nothing; `--timings` restores the line, and `json`, `envelope` and `toon` still carry the timings.

Python `Record.data()` converts like the Neo4j Python driver: a node or relationship becomes the `dict` of its properties and a path a list alternating node property dicts and relationship types, where 1.0.0 returned the `Node`, `Relationship` and `Path` objects; `to_dict()` keeps ids, labels and endpoints.

`shortestPath(…)` outside a `MATCH` needs both end nodes bound, else `syntax error: InvalidPatternCharacter: A shortestPath(...) requires bound nodes when not part of a MATCH clause.`, and refuses a property map on its relationship.

A `MERGE` whose properties read the entity it merges, such as `MERGE (p:Person {name: 'Ida', nick: p.name})`, fails with `syntax error: SyntaxError: Entity, 'p', cannot be created and referenced in the same clause` (exit code 6), where 1.0.0 ran it with deprecation notification `01N00`.

Reading a point component the point does not carry, such as `latitude` on a cartesian point or `z` on a 2D point, fails with `semantic error: Field: latitude is not available on a point value`, even behind a false `WHERE` condition on the point's `srid`; 1.0.0 returned `y` for `latitude`, `x` for `longitude` and `null` for a missing `z`, and a `CASE` on the SRID guards the read.

A Bolt message over the 262,144 decoded-value limit fails its request with `Neo.ClientError.Request.Invalid` and a message naming the size, the limit and the remedy, and the connection serves the next request after `RESET`; 1.0.0 closed the connection.
The install script, `install.sh`, downloads every release asset from `https://github.com/relatedb/relate/releases/download/…`, with no GitHub API request and no token.

releases.summary: The first stable release, and the first published to PyPI (`relate-db`), npm (`@relate/relate`, `@relate/relate-wasm`) and crates.io (`relate`). The Rust crate's change-data-capture methods are removed, and messages no longer cite internal design records.

added.text: The clients are on their registries at the release's version: `pip install relate-db`, `npm install @relate/relate` (with its platform package) and `@relate/relate-wasm`, and `cargo add relate`. The npm packages carry npm provenance and the PyPI files trusted-publishing attestations. The Java jars stay release downloads.

changed.text: Messages no longer end with an upstream design-record reference: for example `pull writes into an empty database only` and `serve: opened the store read-only — no writer lease …`, where 0.1.3 added `(ADR-0158)` and `(ADR-0306)`.

`relate upgrade` reads only the release list it names, with no fallback host, and its error reads `could not read the release list: GET <url>: <reason>; reinstall manually instead: curl -sSfL https://relatedb.ai/install.sh | bash`; `install.sh` resolves the latest release from `https://relatedb.ai/releases.json` too.
Opening an `s3://` URI reports that object storage belongs to the clients that embed relate.

removed.text: The Rust crate's change-data-capture methods, `register_cdc_slot`, `ack_cdc_slot`, `drop_cdc_slot`, `cdc_slots`, `cdc_records_after`, `set_apply_only` and `apply_only`, and the `CdcSlot` type. A checkpoint no longer keeps WAL segments for a slot, and a `cdc/slots.json` file is ignored. `apply_replicated` stays.

releases.summary: Element ids carry the shorter `rl-id` segment, the Parquet codec always writes typed columns, errors report the class of the stage that raised them, and every spelling of a shortest-path query takes the dedicated shortest-route engine.

added.text: The procedure `dbms.listCapabilities()` answers with four rows on what this engine can do: `cypher.version`, `fulltext.index`, `vector.index` and `pattern.engine`.

Notification `03C94`, `Relate.Notification.Statement.LabelDisjunctionScan`, on an equality on a property of a label disjunction, such as `(p:Model OR p:Source) AND p.id = 1`, that no range index on each label serves; with those indexes the plan's `NodeByLabelSeek` looks the value up once per label.

changed.text: `elementId()` writes the namespace segment as `rl-id`: the first node of the default database is `4:rl-id:n0` and its first relationship `5:rl-id:r0`, where 0.1.2 returned `4:relate-neo4j:n0` and `5:relate-neo4j:r0`. An id in the old spelling matches no entity.

The `parquet` codec always writes a typed column per shared property key (format version `5`, `6` with an ontology), and `--snapshot-format parquet-wide` is no longer a value: it fails with `unknown snapshot format 'parquet-wide'`. A store written at format version `3` or `4` opens, and its next checkpoint rewrites every data file.
`SHOW INDEXES` lists two lookup indexes on every store, `index_460996c0` on node labels and `index_1b9dcc97` on relationship types; they can't be dropped and the schema copy leaves them out.

`SHOW PROCEDURES` lists 31 rows, where 0.1.2 listed 88: the catalog entries for change data capture, server configuration and connections, clustering and routing, fleet management, usage statistics, index resampling and the vector-property setters are gone. A `CALL` to one of them still fails with `ProcedureNotFound`.

Errors report the class of the stage that raised them: a rejection the statement text decides is a `syntax` error (several `USE` targets in one statement included), a function argument out of its domain at run time, such as `range()` with a step of 0, has the kind `argument` and the Bolt code `Neo.ClientError.Statement.ArgumentError`, a `DELETE` of a node with relationships begins `ConstraintVerificationFailed: DeleteConnectedNode:`, and a float `SKIP` or `LIMIT` adds `, got FLOAT` to its message.
The Go and Swift clients type a notification's severity and category (`Severity`, `Category`) and refuse a value outside them; 0.1.2 used plain strings.
The Node.js client's platform packages are `@relate/relate-<platform>-<arch>`, such as `@relate/relate-darwin-arm64`.
The Python client's `element_id` values are always strings; a graph value from the `system` namespace raises `RuntimeError` instead of carrying `None`.

Every spelling of a shortest-path query, the `shortestPath()` expression, `SHORTEST k` selectors and quantified relationships included, takes the dedicated shortest-route engine, and a `MATCH` with OR'd labels and a key predicate is served as a union of per-label seeks.

releases.summary: Element ids carry the database's name, and a shortest path between two endpoints matched by property maps is searched from both ends.

changed.text: `elementId()` names the database: the first node of the default database is `4:relate-neo4j:n0` and its first relationship `5:relate-neo4j:r0`, where 0.1.1 returned `4:relate:n0` and `5:relate:r0`, and the clients, JSON output and Bolt carry the same strings.
A `shortestPath` whose two endpoints are matched by property maps looks up both endpoints and searches from both ends at once.
Opening a store whose write-ahead log replays nothing no longer rebuilds its indexes.
`relate upgrade` no longer prints the notice of the rename after its status line.

releases.summary: Full-text search reads the index's query syntax and ranks by BM25, and the Parquet codec can store each promoted property in a column of its own.

added.text: `--snapshot-format parquet-wide`, on a query run and on `relate serve`, which gains the flag: the Parquet codec writes one typed column per promoted property key, and from the store's next checkpoint on every later open keeps it wide.
Full-text search pages with `SKIP` and `OFFSET`, and `WITH ANALYZER` is evaluated per row, English stemming included.

changed.text: Full-text search passes the query string to the index's query syntax, so `AND` and `NOT` are operators while a lowercase `and` stays a term, and it ranks hits by BM25 scores, so a hit's `score` and the order of hits can differ from 0.1.0.
The Java client's `QueryType`, `Namespace`, `Severity` and `Category` are enums instead of strings, and `PlanActual` carries the whole plan shape.
POINT indexes seek radius and bounding-box queries through an R*-tree.
The variable-shadowing notification also looks inside the bodies of `EXISTS`, `COUNT` and `COLLECT` subqueries.

fixed.text: `round()` on a decimal, the sort order of temporal values, and the type of a nested list whose elements have mixed types.
A list value at a `WHERE` or `FILTER` position is coerced to a predicate.
`FINISH` is accepted after a catalog command that returns rows, and a schema command runs only as a statement of its own.

releases.summary: The first release published as relate, which restarts the version line at 0.1.0 after cypherlite's 0.16.1: the release assets are `relate-<os>-<arch>` and `relate-ffi-<target>.tar.gz`, and the signer and the signature namespace are `relate-release`, with the same key.

added.text: Every machine-readable result carries per-phase timings and the plan cache's outcome: `--mode envelope` and `--mode json` add a `timings` object and `planCache`, `--mode jsonl` ends each statement with a line holding both, `--mode toon` ends with `timings:` and `planCache:` entries, the envelope of MCP and the WebAssembly build adds `lex_parse_ms`, `rewrite_ms`, `lower_ms`, `result_generation_ms` and `plan_cache`, and the Rust crate's `QueryResult` adds the same four timings and `plan_cache()`; the C ABI and the other clients expose none of them yet.
The `FOR` clause runs without a preview gate.

changed.text: `--mode json` prints an object for every statement, `{"data": [...], "planCache": ..., "timings": {...}}`, where 0.16.1 printed a bare array for a result the row cap did not cut.
`--mode jsonl` prints one more line per statement, its timings, so a statement with no rows prints that one line instead of nothing.

`relate clone` refuses a `markdown` store as the source of a `.rl` bundle unless `--to-snapshot-format` names `parquet` or `json`, with `Failed to clone database: semantic error: markdown body properties are set but the store's snapshot codec is parquet, not markdown; the configuration would be ignored`.

Usage metrics are written to a local spool at exit and sent by the next run, so an exit never waits on the network, and `RELATE_TELEMETRY_FLUSH_MS` is removed; `relate telemetry off` deletes the spool.

fixed.text: `coll.max()` returns null when the list holds a null, as Neo4j does.
`toString()` of a path and an index into a null string return what Neo4j returns.
A count-style aggregate over a repeated node variable counts only self-loops.
In the Swift client, `transaction(_:)` rolls back when `commit()` throws.

releases.summary: The last release published under the name cypherlite: its release assets carry that name, and a successful `cypherlite upgrade` ends with a notice of the rename and the relate install command.

changed.text: The C ABI is the typed ABI v2: `relate_abi_version()` returns 2, values are read through typed accessors instead of JSON strings, parameters are passed through a typed builder instead of a JSON string, and an error arrives as one object with `code`, `gql_status`, `stage`, `retryable` and `message`.
The Python binding and the Java, JavaScript, Go and Swift clients use the typed ABI v2.
The typed parameter builder is bounded: at most 100,000 entries per container, 4 KiB per name, and 16 MiB in all.
A bookmark carries the engine's commit sequence, through the C ABI, Python and Bolt.
An error of the internal class crosses the C ABI with a generic message; the internal detail stays inside the engine.
A non-boolean value where Cypher requires a boolean, such as a quantifier's `WHERE` or an operand of `AND`, `OR` or `XOR`, fails with `InvalidArgumentType` instead of a generic syntax error.

A clause that reads an entity it creates fails with `Entity, '<name>', cannot be created and referenced in the same clause`, and a `CREATE` or `MERGE` whose node is bound to null fails instead of creating a new node.
An administration command with a `USE` clause that names a graph other than `system` fails with `UseClauseWithAdministrationCommand`.

removed.text: The `apoc.coll.sort` spelling: a call fails as an unknown function, `UnknownFunction: unknown function apoc.coll.sort()`, and `coll.sort` is the replacement.

fixed.text: A frontier search that exhausts its re-arrival budget falls back to the plain walk instead of dropping endpoints, which could make `count(DISTINCT n)` return 0 on a dense clique.
`push` keeps a node's secondary labels and merges on its keyed label, so an update no longer creates a second node.
